bibliography.note: Deeds, J., Amirbahman, A., Hugger, K., Kaufmann, P. R., Matthews, L. J., Merrell, K. & Norton, S. A. 2023. Assessment indices of littoral habitat condition for lakes in Maine and New England, United States. Lake and Reservoir Management 39(2): 141–155, doi:10.1080/10402381.2023.2207490 — as cited

claims.claim: Maine surveyed the littoral substrate of 102 lakes in 2007–2019 (Deeds et al. 2023)
claims.location: web page (single HTML page), Methods: 'Study lakes' and 'Habitat condition models'
claims.conditions: 'Lakes included in this analysis were surveyed between 2007 and 2019'; the Maine set combines the EPA's National Lakes Assessment surveys of Maine lakes (2007, 2012, 2017; randomly drawn plus EPA reference lakes) with Maine state-level surveys of hand-picked larger and more developed lakes; NLA physical-habitat protocol: 10 shore stations per lake, each a 10 × 15 m littoral plot with cover classes (Maine split the 10–40 % class into 10–25 and 25–40 %)
claims.note: strictly, not all 102 were surveyed by Maine: part are NLA (US EPA) surveys of Maine lakes

claims.claim: The published analysis gives model coefficients rather than cover values; in it, sand cover rises with shoreland disturbance
claims.quote: percent sand cover (SUB_SAND), which increased with shoreland disturbance
claims.conditions: SUB_SAND was in all six linear-discriminant models; the article tabulates metric definitions, model performance and LDA coefficients and plots lake scores; no table of substrate cover values; the metric-versus-disturbance plots are in supplementary Figure S3 (not seen)
claims.note: The authors say sandy littorals may be natural (preferred for houses), eroded from development, or added for beaches. The check covers the article only; the supplement may show sand-cover values against the disturbance score.

claims.claim: Maine's 102-lake survey scored woody habitat but did not publish values (Deeds et al. 2023)
claims.quote: Large woody habitat (>30 cm diameter) cover
claims.conditions: woody-habitat metrics (FC_LWH, FC_SWH, total woody habitat, littoral woody habitat, the Habitat Complexity Index) enter the models as cover classes; no woody-habitat values per lake or per station are given in the article
claims.note: as above, the supplement was not seen

notes: Context for §3.2.7–3.2.8: 70 % of Maine lakes are ≤ 10 ha; in the NLA the northeastern lakes showed poor lakeshore and littoral habitat linked to reduced riparian vegetation; 24 % of the study's lakeshore stations had buildings or lawns in or beside the riparian plot. Lakes were grouped Deep/Shallow at 10 m maximum depth. The supplement (Figures S1–S3) would be the place to look for any sand or wood cover values.
